what: The merged-versus-baked PDD8 pair, the first render of the backbone bake lane (docs/research/pdd/2026-09-05_bake_plan.md). One new arm per scene: PDD8 on the baked fl2va checkpoint with the stripped sidecar, sage on every step, Sol absent (h3_probe_t2v_pdd8_baked_sage). Its merged twin, h3_probe_t2v_pdd8_sage, was rendered on 2026-09-04 as the PDD ladder's pdd8sage rung on the same scenes at the same seed, and is reused as the reference rather than re-rendered; the two graphs differ only in the checkpoint and the sidecar, so the pair differs in whether the PDD backbone delta reached the weights through a requantised merge at load or was quantised once with them. Hypothesis under test, written in docs/roadmap.md's bake paragraph: the defects the owner named blind on the shipped PDD8 rung are the kind a requantised merge produces. Same five scenes, same seed, 1344x768, 345 frames; judged blind.

rungs.pdd8baked: PDD8 on MODELS['unet_fl2va_pdd8_baked'] with PDD_FL2VA_STRIPPED_LORA, sage auto on every step, Sol absent (h3_probe_t2v_pdd8_baked_sage). The node enforces the checkpoint-sidecar pairing by content at load.

prompts: named by bank id through the runner's @bank: value; the text lives only in prompt_bank/
reference_rows: two per scene, appended to this run's JSONL before blinding so blind_batch.py can pair them by run index: the <scene>_pdd8sage rows of bench/results/2026-09-04_pdd_ladder_arms_judged.jsonl (the merged twin, rendered 2026-09-04 on a post-pull server, seed 730451892) and the <scene>_sage rows of bench/results/2026-09-03_ladder_arms_judged.jsonl (the sage 16-step floor). The pdd8sage pair is same-regime if the server code has not changed since 2026-09-04; the sage pair is cross-regime as the PDD ladder's was.
run: python bench/run_graph_arms.py --manifest bench/pdd_bake_arms.json --runs 1 --seed 730451892 --hold-seed --no-alternate --warmup standoff_pdd8baked --out bench/results/<date>_pdd_bake_arms.jsonl; append the ten reference rows named above; then bench/blind_batch.py on that JSONL with, per scene, --pairs <scene>_pdd8sage,<scene>_pdd8baked --pairs <scene>_sage,<scene>_pdd8baked; score pairs AND singles; bench/score_session.py.

pairs_that_are_controlled.pdd8sage vs pdd8baked: the bake's effect alone: same graph family, same steps, same kernels, same seed, checkpoint and sidecar the only difference. The primary question and the test of the roadmap's bake hypothesis.
pairs_that_are_controlled.sage (ladder, 16 steps) vs pdd8baked: is PDD8 on the bake as good as the sage floor; cross-regime, see reference_rows

how_to_read: within a scene only. One seed per arm, so each contest is one stack judged once. Free text over scales: say what differs and which way, naming the four defects from the shipped rung where they appear. Score the singles: they carry the audio, and the owner reported PDD audio quieter on the 2026-09-03 ladder.
cost: reasoned, not measured: the same eight sage steps as pdd8sage; the bake changes weights, not work. Nothing at load either, since no backbone patch is applied. Any timing is in the post-pull regime and is compared only with rows from that regime.
requires: a ComfyUI server up with this pack's graphs regenerated against the live /object_info; the baked checkpoint linked into models/diffusion_models and the stripped sidecar in models/loras/h3 (docs/pdd_artifacts.md).
generated_by: workflows/build_workflows.py for the probe graph; regenerate there, never edit the graph
policy: sage always on (owner decision 2026-09-04); the pair is rendered under sage alone so Sol is not in the comparison
